note.p: Godwin was brought up in part by a cousin of his father's, a Miss Hannah Godwin who became Mrs George Sothren, of whom Godwin had fond memories. George dies in 1785 and Mrs Sothren in December 1796. But there are references to Sothren in the Diary linked to this member of the family.

Ed Pope suggests: Probably George Sothren baptised Norwich 1762 son of George and Hannah (nee Raimes, married Norwich 1754). His father, probably a tailor of Norwich who voted there in 1768 and 1780, married Godwin's cousin Hannah at Gaiswick (i.e.Guestwick) 15.9.1772 and died 29.8.1785 (Abinger c.1 f.28-9). Mrs Sothren died 22.12.1796 (c.14 f.112). A George Sothern was apprenticed 1776 to Robert Priest druggist of Norwich and married Margaret Cook Trull at St Peter Mancroft on 14.1.1794, and he or his son George born c.1795 voted as chemist or druggist in Norwich between 1796 and 1832. On 19.12.1799 Godwin's mother wrote to him 'I will send you by Mr Sothren' (c.5 f41). The three entries in 1794 follow Mrs Sothren on 27.6.94 and could refer to her or her stepson, indeed perhaps they lived together. A letter of Amelia Alderson's (Abinger c.3 f.16v) dated 5.2.1796 refers to Mrs Sothren and her daughter
